name: teleport_short_gap10
drive_hint: held_tone(node_ids=[left terminal of stroke A, at (0,0)], frequency=0.02, amplitude=1.0, attack_steps=300, duration_steps=2500). Compiler detects a single coupler between the two lines (gap=10px, kappa~0.436, coupler lowpass coef~0.273).
notes: Gap must satisfy 8px (SNAP_EPS) < gap < 30px (COUPLER_G_MAX) or the parser either fuses the strokes into one node (gap<8) or no coupler forms at all (gap>=30, hard cutoff, not a fade). At gap=10 with default ink both sides, 21.6% of driven energy shows up as radiated energy on the untouched stroke B's terminals -- a clearly readable 'wireless junction' teleport, not noise. Tighten the gap toward 8.5px for a stronger ~26% tunneled fraction; widen toward 20-25px for a faint/unreliable effect. Low frequencies (0.01-0.02 cyc/sample) tunnel roughly 4-8x better than high ones (0.1-0.15) at the same gap -- 'blink range' should read as a frequency knob, not a fixed number.

name: overcharge_loop_r30
drive_hint: held_tone(node_ids=[the loop's single open-tail terminal, at (70,0)], frequency=f0, amplitude=A, attack_steps=300, duration_steps>=3000) where f0 = 1/round(loop_circumference/dx) ~= 0.02128 cyc/sample (2.13 Hz game-frequency) for this radius-30 loop -- read it off sim.network's longest edge (the self-closing loop edge) rather than hardcoding it, since it shifts with radius/dx. Sweep A from ~0.05 up to ~2.0.
notes: This shape (loop_with_tail_points, radius=30, tail=40) puts f0 almost exactly on filter-bank band[1] (0.0209) and 2*f0 almost exactly on band[2] (0.0437), so the thermal-band response to the 2nd harmonic is cleanly visible in the analyzer, not just in a raw FFT. IMPORTANT measurement caveat: a short/broadband tap on this small high-Q loop rings up a 2nd-harmonic resonant mode on its own, with NO nonlinearity involved (confirmed: linear-ink 2nd/1st harmonic ratio sits flat at ~5.77 regardless of drive amplitude) -- always drive with a sustained held_tone at exactly f0 and compare against a linear-ink control (nl_threshold=1e6) at the same amplitude; only the EXCESS over that baseline is real overcharge. With nl_threshold=1.0/nl_asymmetry=0.35 (recommended middle ground) expect the thermal/kinetic ratio to clear +15-20% over baseline by amplitude ~0.3-0.5. A hotter ink (nl_threshold=0.5, nl_asymmetry=0.4) turns on earlier (+34% by amplitude 0.2) but self-limits and drops BELOW baseline past amplitude ~0.5-0.7 -- a real skill ceiling, not a bug, worth keeping as a distinct 'volatile' ink tier.

name: phase_kinetic_displacement
drive_hint: NOT a single tap/tone -- inject a SUM of two sine components at the single open terminal (x=0 end), each with a shared linear attack ramp over 150 steps: sample(i) = attack(i) * (1.0*sin(2*pi*0.015*i) + 3.0*sin(2*pi*0.38*i)). The 0.015 cyc/sample component is the deliberate kinetic ingredient (low band); the 0.38 cyc/sample component (near Nyquist, lands on filter-bank band[5], weight 1.0 in PHASE_BAND_WEIGHTS) is the deliberate phase ingredient. Track with Sim's per-step drives['phase']/['kinetic'] fed into Token.apply_phase / apply_kinetic_impulse manually (not Sim.apply_world_coupling's default giant arena -- use a realistic tight bounds Rect to actually see collision get skipped).
notes: With this drive, token phase crosses PHASE_GHOST_THRESHOLD=0.5 at step 56 (t=0.56s) while position is only 3.6px from start -- well before reaching any wall placed even a modest distance away. The token keeps accelerating under the kinetic component while ghosted and passes straight through a wall placed at x=60 at step 104, phase still ~0.994 (fully ghosted). CAUTION / balance finding: KINETIC_BAND_WEIGHTS's top band weight is 0.03 (not 0), and apply_world_coupling scales kinetic by 40000 vs phase's 40 (1000x) -- so even a phase-tone-ONLY drive (zero deliberate low-frequency component) still produces enough incidental kinetic push to reach the same wall only ~25% later on its own. If the design wants phase+kinetic to read as a genuine two-ingredient combo rather than 'just drive it hard enough', either zero the top entry of KINETIC_BAND_WEIGHTS or shrink the kinetic_scale/phase_scale ratio.

name: parry_y_junction
drive_hint: This mechanic needs a genuine two-part timed drive, not a single tap -- use dual_tap directly rather than folding it into one scenario tap. Stroke 0 ends at (-250,0) = the 'attack' terminal (incoming enemy energy). Stroke 1 ends at (-216.51,125) = the 'defense' terminal (the player's parry ignition point). Stroke 2 runs from the shared junction (0,0) out to (216.51,-125) = the 'world' terminal, whose radiated energy is what you're defending. Call dual_tap(node_ids_a=[attack_terminal], node_ids_b=[defense_terminal], amplitude=1.0, burst_len=24, delay_steps=D, sign_b=-1.0). All three branches are drawn the same length (250px, ~61-64 samples at dx=4) so attack and defense arrive at the junction simultaneously at D=0 -- that IS the 'half a wavelength of extra path' the design doc describes, just expressed as a direct time delay instead of drawn geometry (the player could equally draw the defense stroke slightly longer/shorter to shift D by whole samples).
notes: Measured at the world terminal: attack alone radiates 0.06515884 (baseline). Correct parry (delay_steps=0, sign_b=-1.0, equal branch lengths) cancels it to exactly 0.0 (machine precision) because the junction's admittance-weighted scatter sums Y*u from all three edges and Y_attack*u_attack + Y_defense*u_defense = 0 when the ink (hence Z, hence Y) matches and the waves are equal-and-opposite at the moment they meet. A defense mistimed by 20% of burst_len (delay_steps=5) only cancels about half (0.0317, 49% of baseline). Mistimed by a full burst_len or more (delay_steps>=24) does NOT cancel at all -- worse, it's 2x WORSE than no defense at all (0.130), because the inverted burst arrives after the attack has already passed and independently radiates its own energy. Using the correct timing but forgetting to invert (sign_b=+1.0) is worse still: 4x baseline (waves reinforce, (2A)^2 scaling). IMPORTANT bug caveat: dual_tap's injections dict silently OVERWRITES rather than sums when node_ids_a and node_ids_b share a node id and their bursts overlap in time -- keep attack and defense on physically distinct terminals (as here) so the interference happens for real in the network's own junction scattering, not in a Python dict.
